# Heatmap of the hourly averages of one sensor

A column per day and a row per hour of the day, from midnight at the
top, each colored by the average of that hour, so that what happens at
the same time every day shows as a horizontal band. The colors stop at
the 2nd and 98th percentiles, so that a few spikes do not wash out the
rest; the hover label has the exact value.

## Usage

``` r
plot_daily_pattern(hourly, variable, unit = "", mode = "light", mid = NULL)
```

## Arguments

- hourly:

  Data frame from
  [`get_hourly()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/golemenviro/reference/get_hourly.md).

- variable:

  Name of the sensor, for the title and the hover labels.

- unit:

  Unit of the readings, `""` for none.

- mode:

  `"light"` or `"dark"`, the mode of the app.

- mid:

  A value to color white, with lower values in blue and higher values in
  red, such as room temperature; the color range is then made symmetric
  around it. `NULL` (the default) for one blue, from light to dark.

## Value

A plotly object.

## Examples

``` r
hourly <- expand.grid(hour = 0:23, date = as.Date("2026-10-01") + 0:13)
hourly$value <- 21 + 2 * sin((hourly$hour - 9) / 24 * 2 * pi)
plot_daily_pattern(hourly, "Temperature", "C")
```
